newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM calls for U.N. to investigate attack.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM calls for U.N. to investigate attack.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh called on Saturday for the United Nations to investigate a deadly grenade attack against an opposition rally in Phnom Penh.

"I would like the Ministry of Interior to continue (its investigation), but at the same time I will... ask the United Nations to send a team for investigation of the case," Ranariddh told reporters at a memorial ceremony for victims of the blast.
On March 30, four grenades were thrown into a demonstration led by opposition leader Sam Rainsy, killing as many as 19 people and injuring more than 100.
The apparent target Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury, has blamed co-premier Hun Sen for the attack. Hun Sen has denied responsibility.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, have agreed to a joint interior ministry investigation into the incident, which both men condemned.
Earlier in the week Ranariddh called for an independent inquiry led by Cambodians, a call he repeated on Saturday by recommending a National Assembly probe.
But for the first time he also called for U.N. involvement.
David Hawk, director of the U.N. Centre for Human Rights in Cambodia, said: "If there is a request, we'll consider it". He said he could not comment further before seeing the request.
Ranariddh has said he also wants the U.N. to provide observers for coming elections, which are likely to pit his FUNCINPEC party against Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP).

He described the grenade attack as the onset of intimidation and violence ahead of the polls. "I fear there will not really be free and fair elections," he said. Local elections are due this year and national polls in 1998.
Meanwhile, tensions in the capital continued to simmer after four armoured personnel carriers rolled through Phnom Penh on Friday to protect the house of Hun Sen.
In an apparent reference to his troubled relationship with Hun Sen, Ranariddh told reporters, "Ideologically speaking, I feel much closer to Sam Rainsy than someone else."

Sam Rainsy, scheduled to leave for a three-week trip to France and the United States late on Saturday, said FUNCINPEC was planning to provide him with strong protection in case the CPP tried to stop him from leaving the country.
